day.reading: Duffy: not the waiting-time problem; an empirical audit of observable fixations, better called the fixation problem
day.holds: in form F_max has no mutation-rate input (Hancock says the same, G2h q1); it counts fixations from an observed rate, not arrivals

critic.reading: Matthews: still a waiting-time problem, since in creationist usage the waiting-time problem is a fixation problem and the two rates are used interchangeably (Axe)
critic.holds: the observed G_f MITTENS divides by includes the wait for mutations to arise in a clonal population, which Day concedes ('worst-case scenario', evo005@L16; kappa 93,659, M-103), so arrival waiting is inside the input; Hancock's lineage claim is a family resemblance (F1c)

notes: Inference, classification only; no number is printed in the rows. The two sides use 'waiting-time problem' in different senses: Duffy's is mutation arrival; Matthews's is the creationist usage in which it is a fixation problem. Under Duffy's sense the formula is not one (no mutation rate); under Matthews's sense the label fits, and the LTEE input carries arrival waiting either way. The Axe attribution is not checked (abstract only). The rate-vs-distribution point is M-101; transfer is M-103.
